info.title: FetchX API
info.description:
FetchX gets any public URL and returns its data. POST /v1/fetch does the work, and POST /v1/fetch/{id}/next gets the page after one; POST /v1/estimate says what a request or a batch would cost and take before you send it; the other endpoints read results, download files, list, delete and report credits. GET /v1/status needs no key.

Two status layers: the HTTP code says whether FetchX accepted the call; the `status` field says what happened to the fetch. A fetch that ran and failed is HTTP 200 with `status: failed`. A pending fetch is HTTP 202. A 4xx means the request itself was wrong, nothing was sent to the site and nothing was charged.

Billing: a request is charged only when it succeeds, at the price of the step that got the data. Failed, uncertain and refused requests cost nothing, and so does a page that loads without what `expect` asked for. Every result says what it cost in `credits`, with a breakdown.

Changes are listed at https://fetchx.ai/changelog (info.version is the latest release). A deprecated route carries Deprecation, Sunset and Link headers until its sunset date; a retired route answers 410 with error.code route_retired and error.details.replacement; an unknown route answers 404 with error.code route_not_found and links to the docs, the changelog and the status page. While maintenance pauses the API, every route except GET /v1/status answers 503 with error.code maintenance, a Retry-After header and error.details.status_url (https://fetchx.ai/status).

post.description: Gets a URL and returns its data. With only `url`, FetchX climbs from the cheapest route (HTTP direct, datacenter, residential with fresh IPs on a 429, then a browser) until the site gives its real answer, starting at the step that worked for this site before. Only the step that worked is charged. GET and HEAD may use up to `max_attempts` attempts; any other method gets exactly one attempt and never a browser.

post.description:
Gets the page after request {id}'s, as a new request with its own id. Request {id} must have succeeded with a `data.next_page`, and its content must not have expired (7 days) or been deleted.

FetchX builds the new request from the earlier one: the same headers, formats, country, render, wait_for and scroll, plus the cookies the site set on the earlier page. When the earlier page came through a residential browser session, the next page uses the same session (exit IP and device identity) while it is still available, so the site sees the same visitor. For `link`, FetchX fetches the next page's address with the earlier page as referrer. For `click` and `scroll`, it opens the list again, repeats the steps back to the earlier page, then clicks its next control or scrolls further, so each later page of a long list takes a little longer. The new page has its own `data.next_page`, so a list is read by calling this with each new id in turn.

Billed like any request: only when it succeeds, at the price of the step that got the data (a browser step when the next page needs one). A failed next page costs nothing.

post.summary: Estimate cost and time before sending
post.description: What one request, or a batch of up to 1000, would cost and how long it would take, before anything is sent, reserved or charged. Send the body you would send to POST /v1/fetch, or a batch body ({items, defaults}: each item a URL or a request, merged over defaults). For each request FetchX plans the steps it would try and prices them with what recent requests to the same site took (the step that got the data, its traffic, captcha solves and time: learned from every customer's requests by host name only), its price table, your max_credits and your balance. credits.typical is what one success usually costs and credits.high a high-end cost (90th percentile); credits.expected counts only the share of requests that usually succeed, since failures are free; credits.hold is what the request reserves while it runs. basis says where the figures come from: history (this site's recent requests), routes (a route known to work, priced from other sites), defaults (no history: typical figures for the first step) or assumed. A batch's seconds assume FetchX's per-site pace. notes say what to change when a request would be refused or is likely to fail.

post.description: FetchX POSTs the finished result (without the body) to webhook_url. Verify `X-FetchX-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 with the project's webhook secret over `<X-FetchX-Timestamp>.<raw body>`. Delivery is tried 3 times.

ApiKey.description: A project API key (fxk_...), made in the console or by the Connect flow. Each operation lists the scope it needs in x-scope: fetch:write, fetch:read or usage:read.

url.description: The page, API or file to get. Public http or https only: private, local and metadata addresses are refused, checked after DNS and on every redirect.

method.description: Only GET and HEAD escalate. Other methods get one attempt, never a browser, and are never retried.

headers.description: Headers for the site, cookies and Authorization included (stored encrypted, never logged). Up to 64 headers and 16 KB. Host, hop-by-hop, Forwarded and X-Forwarded-* are refused.

body.description: A text request body, up to 1 MB. Only with POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE.

body_base64.description: A binary request body in base64, instead of body.

render.description: auto tries HTTP first and moves to a browser when HTTP is blocked or the page is an empty JavaScript shell; always starts in a browser; never stays on HTTP.

wait_for.description: In a browser, wait for a CSS selector or a fixed time. Implies a browser.

scroll.description: How far a page opened in a browser is scrolled before it is read. auto (the default): once the page has filled in, keep scrolling while scrolling loads more, up to 10 screens. off: read the page once it has filled in, without scrolling. A number from 1 to 50: scroll up to that many screens, stopping early at the end of the page; implies a browser, and more screens take more time (raise timeout_ms for many). Scrolling has no fee of its own, but what a scrolled page loads is traffic like any other: on a residential route it counts toward the per-MB charge beyond the included traffic, so off is the cheapest choice when the first screen is enough. A number past 10 reserves credits for 2.5 MB more traffic a screen while the request runs; only what the page used is charged.

country.description: The exit country for proxy routes (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). Defaults to the country that worked for this site before, else US.

route.description: One fixed route; turns auto mode off: one attempt, with a precise error.

country.description: Required for datacenter and residential; null for direct.

render.description: true uses a browser on this route.

formats.description: What to return. body: the response as received (the rendered page after a browser), the default when formats is left out. markdown, text, links, metadata and json are derived from it; screenshot needs a browser. Ask only for what you use: a rendered page can be megabytes of HTML. The body is stored either way and can be downloaded from /v1/fetch/{id}/content.

block_resources.description: In a browser, do not download images, video, audio or web fonts on the page. They carry none of the text but a good part of a rendered page’s traffic, and residential traffic past the included megabytes is charged per MB; the text and every image URL stay in the page. Captcha widgets still load theirs. Defaults to true, or false when formats has screenshot.

expect.description: What the page must show to be the content you want. Every condition given must hold, or the step is not a success: auto mode tries a browser, then one fresh IP, and a request that never gets it fails with content_missing and is not charged. A browser waits up to 10 s for the selector after the page settles. A real 404 or 410 is the site’s answer and is not checked.

selector.description: A CSS selector that must match at least one element (HTML only).

text.description: Text that must appear in the page’s visible text (or a non-HTML body), ignoring case and spacing.

min_markdown_length.description: The page’s markdown (a non-HTML body’s text) must have at least this many characters.

max_attempts.description: The most attempts that may reach the site. Steps refused before anything is sent do not count.

fix_headers.description: Replace automation User-Agents (curl, python-requests…) with a browser one and add a missing Accept and Accept-Language.

max_credits.description: The most this request may cost. Steps that would cost more are skipped.

timeout_ms.description: Total time for all attempts. A captcha solve can take up to a minute, so the default leaves room for one; a synchronous call still answers 202 after 60 seconds if the request is not finished.

async.description: true answers 202 at once; false waits up to 60 seconds, then answers 202.

webhook_url.description: A public https URL that receives the result when the request finishes.

idempotency_key.description: The same key with the same body returns the same result and is charged once. Generated when absent.

tags.description: Your labels, to filter the list.

NextPageRequest.description: What may change for a next page. Everything else (headers, formats, country, render, wait_for, block_resources) comes from the earlier request, and the cookies the site set on the earlier page are sent with it. An empty object is fine.

scroll.description: As in FetchRequest; defaults to the earlier request's. For a next page that loads as the page is scrolled (next_page.how is scroll), it is how many more screens to scroll past where the earlier page ended (auto: up to 10 more); off is refused there.

expect.description: As in POST /v1/fetch. Left out, the earlier request's expect applies; null drops it, for a list whose later pages do not show what the first one did.

selector.description: A CSS selector that must match at least one element (HTML only).

text.description: Text that must appear in the page’s visible text (or a non-HTML body), ignoring case and spacing.

min_markdown_length.description: The page’s markdown (a non-HTML body’s text) must have at least this many characters.

max_credits.description: The most this page may cost. Not taken from the earlier request: without it, the page may use any step, like a new request. A next page holds credits for the deepest page's traffic (150 MB) while it runs and is charged only for what it used; max_credits caps both.

timeout_ms.description: As in FetchRequest; defaults to the earlier request's. A next page reached by clicking or scrolling opens the list again and repeats the earlier steps first, so deep pages of a long list may need more time.

idempotency_key.description: The same key with the same body returns the same result and is charged once. Generated when absent.

page_status.description: What the page was. content: the page you asked for (with expect, it showed what you expected). not_found: the site’s real 404 or 410, billed like content. empty: it loaded but showed next to nothing, or not what expect asked for. challenge: a bot wall, block or rate limit stopped it (see challenge). error: anything else (see error). Null while pending.

data.description: What the site answered: on success the real answer, on failure the last response. Null only when nothing reached the site.

challenge.description: The walls the request met on its way, or null when it met none.

credits.description: What this request cost. Present on every result: a pending or failed request shows 0.

charged.description: 0 unless the request succeeded. Never more than max.

max.description: The most this request could have cost: max_credits, or the dearest step it might use (null for unmetered projects).

balance.description: Credits the project has available as this answer is made (null for unmetered projects). Also at GET /v1/balance.

breakdown.description: How the price of the step that got the data adds up; null unless the request succeeded.

attempts.description: One entry per step tried, in order. Providers are never named.

skipped.description: Steps that were not tried, and why.

Challenge.description: Blocks, bot challenges and rate limits met on the way, and on the page that answered (a captcha, a wall that cleared). FetchX handles them itself; this says what it met and how it got past.

vendor.description: The bot-protection vendor last seen (datadome, cloudflare, akamai, imperva, human, aws_waf, recaptcha, hcaptcha), or null when the page did not say.

passed.description: Whether FetchX got past them to the page.

passed_by.description: rotation: a later attempt on another route or a fresh IP got through; captcha: solved on the page (10 credits); wait: it cleared by itself. Null when not passed.

CreditBreakdown.description: charged = step_credits + captcha_credits + traffic_credits, capped at max.

captcha_credits.description: For a captcha solved on the page, else 0.

traffic_mb.description: Megabytes (10^6 bytes) the step moved, to one decimal.

included_mb.description: Traffic included in a residential step’s price; null when traffic is not charged.

traffic_credits.description: Per started MB past included_mb, on residential steps. block_resources keeps it down.

rendered.description: True when a browser produced the result.

content_expired.description: True after 7 days or DELETE: everything below is gone.

cookies.description: Cookies the site set, for multi-step flows.

next_page.description: On successful results: how the page leads on, or null when FetchX found no next page. Gone with the rest of the content after 7 days or DELETE.

body.description: The body: utf-8 text, or base64 for binary. Only when formats has body (the default); left out on reads with include_body=false, and when it is too large to inline (see body_url).

body_url.description: Where to download a body too large to inline.

json.description: formats: json, the body parsed as JSON (null when it is not JSON).

screenshot.description: formats: screenshot, base64 JPEG. Also at /v1/fetch/{id}/screenshot.

PageInfo.description: Where this page sits in a list read page by page, and how far it was scrolled.

number.description: 1 for a request made with POST /v1/fetch; each next page adds 1.

previous_id.description: The request this one is the next page of; null for page 1.

screens.description: Screens scrolled reading this page (for a next page that loads on scroll, past where the earlier page ended). 0 when it was not scrolled.

end.description: true: scrolling reached the end of the page and nothing more loaded. false: scrolling stopped (screens or time) while there was more. null: not scrolled.

NextPage.description: How a page leads on to the next one. Open it with POST /v1/fetch/{id}/next.

how.description: link: a link to the next page (url). click: a Next or Load more control the page handles itself, with no address of its own. scroll: the list loads more as it is scrolled further, and scrolling stopped before its end.

url.description: For link: the next page's address.

rotation.description: A fresh residential IP for the same step.

result.description: not_admitted means nothing reached the site on this step (for example the provider refused the host); it does not count as an attempt. content_missing means the page loaded without what expect asked for.

code.description: The underlying error, when result is not_admitted or failed.

challenge.description: On a blocked or rate-limited step, the bot-protection vendor whose page it was, when known (for example datadome, cloudflare, akamai, imperva, human, aws_waf).

missing.description: On a content_missing step, the expect conditions the page did not meet.

wire_bytes.description: Bytes this step moved over the network, requests and responses together. On a residential route this is the traffic billed past the included megabytes.

captcha.description: Captchas met on this step, as type:outcome.

warmup.description: Browser steps on sites that have refused FetchX before start at the site's home page. passed: it loaded; cleared: a bot check there cleared by itself; challenged: the check stayed, so this step ended there and the next one used a fresh IP; failed: the home page did not load, and the page was visited directly.

wall.description: A bot check on the page itself: whether it cleared by itself before any captcha was solved.

content.description: Browser steps on pages that answered: settled when the page had stopped filling itself in (results, listings loaded by script) before it was read; still_loading when FetchX's wait ran out first, so the page may be missing content that loads late. Pass wait_for with a selector for what you need to wait longer.

reason.description: For example excluded_by_provider_rule, over_max_credits or cooling.

next.description: What to do next. A request key replays its first result, failures included, so a retry always needs a new idempotency_key.

retry_after_seconds.description: The earliest time a retry can help.

retry_with_new_key.description: true: the same request may succeed if sent again with a new idempotency_key (after retry_after_seconds when given). false: sent again unchanged it would fail the same way; change it as action says.

credits.description: Available now: what new requests can reserve. Null for an unmetered project.

reserved.description: Held by running requests; released or charged when they finish.

purchased.description: Credits bought. They do not expire.

payment_hold.description: True while spending is paused over a payment issue.

EstimateRequest.description: One POST /v1/fetch body, or a batch body: items (URLs, or requests with url) merged over defaults. async, webhook_url and idempotency_key are set once for a batch, never in defaults or an item.

items.description: URLs, or POST /v1/fetch bodies (with url) merged over defaults.

defaults.description: POST /v1/fetch fields every item gets unless it sets its own (not url, async, webhook_url or idempotency_key).

expected.description: typical times the share of requests that usually succeed (failures are free).

high.description: A high-end cost for a success (90th percentile of traffic, with a captcha if the site sometimes needs one).

hold.description: Items only: what the request reserves while it runs (released when it settles).

code.description: no_history, likely_needs_more_credits, likely_needs_other_options, max_credits_too_low, insufficient_credits, balance_may_run_out, balance_limits_pace (a batch), cooling_down, low_success_rate or no_route.

message.description: What it means and what to change.

index.description: The request's position (0 for a single request).

basis.description: Where the figures come from; none when no step is open to this request.

samples.description: Recent requests to this host the figures are based on.

step.description: The step most likely to get the data.

steps.description: The steps likely to get the data, with their share.

planned.description: The steps FetchX would try, in order.

success_rate.description: Share of recent requests to this host that succeeded; null without history.

error.description: Why POST /v1/fetch (or the batch) would refuse this request; it is left out of the totals.

estimated.description: Requests that would be accepted and are in the totals.

credits.description: Credits available now; null for a project that is not metered.

hosts.description: Batches only: per site, its requests, FetchX's pace for it and its credits.

status.description: The worst state of any component.

notices.description: Scheduled and active notices, then those resolved in the last 14 days.

version.description: The API's version (the latest changelog release).

pause_api.description: While active, the API answers 503 maintenance.
